note: Context-length tuning session, TASK-qos-fair-share.md follow-up. All requests through a Kubernetes exec into the vLLM pod itself, hitting localhost:8000 directly (no PAT/AI Gateway/EPP hop). max-num-seqs stayed at 2 throughout.

gpu_memory_utilization_ceiling_probe.note: Binary search on gpu-memory-utilization with max-model-len=84672 fixed, to find the real headroom on this card before picking 0.94.

0.95.error: ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (30.2/31.84 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.95, 30.25 GiB).

short_prompt_benchmark.method: Same methodology as docs/operations/evidence/vllm-benchmark-2026-09-04.json: 25-27 token synthetic prompt, ignore_eos=true, max_tokens=512 (all requests hit finish_reason=length, i.e. genuinely decoded 512 tokens each), temperature=0, streaming with usage, enable_thinking=false. 3 sequential single requests then 2 concurrent requests, run from an idle server.
short_prompt_benchmark.reading: Raising max-model-len 84672->131072 and gpu-memory-utilization 0.90->0.94 costs ~6-12% single-request decode throughput on its own (71->66.6 tok/s), consistent with larger block-table/CUDA-graph padding at longer max-model-len. Enabling kv-offloading-size=8 on top costs a further ~5-6% on single requests (66.6->62.5 tok/s) from the connector's per-step bookkeeping, but is within noise on the 2-concurrent case (61.5 vs 61.9 tok/s) -- the offload connector's overhead is a near-fixed per-step cost that shows up more clearly when GPU compute itself is cheap (short context, single request) than when it is already the bottleneck (2 concurrent requests).

long_context_concurrent_stress_test.method: Two concurrent chat completions with distinct ~110-117k token synthetic prompts (different filler text so they do not share a prefix-cache hit), max_tokens=64, ignore_eos=true, temperature=0, run against the 131072/0.94/offload-8GiB config. Combined prompt tokens (~228k) sit right at the 230,104-token GPU KV pool.
long_context_concurrent_stress_test.reading: Both requests completed successfully (finish_reason=length, no errors, no crash, no restart) with a combined live context (~228k tokens) that exceeds the raw GPU-resident KV pool (230,104 tokens) once max-num-seqs=2 concurrency is accounted for at this max-model-len. kv_offload_load_bytes_total went from 0 to ~513MB during the run: the CPU offload buffer was genuinely read from, i.e. some of request 1's evicted-then-needed blocks were reloaded from CPU RAM instead of being recomputed. Decode speed at this real long context (27-45 tok/s) is well below the short-prompt figures above -- expected, since attention cost during decode scales with context length, not a regression from the tuning itself. TTFT for the second request (48.4s) reflects two ~115k-token prefills sharing max-num-batched-tokens=8192 chunked-prefill slots on one GPU, not KV eviction cost.

node_memory_after_stress_test.note: PyTorch's CUDA caching allocator does not release memory back to the driver after a burst, so free GPU memory measured via nvidia-smi is tighter after real long-context load than at idle. This is expected allocator behavior, not a leak; smoke test and /health stayed green throughout.
